req.title: Login required for create
req.statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they attempt GET /create.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-012 requires that anonymous (unauthenticated) users who attempt GET /create are redirected to /auth/login with a 302 status. Three test cases are designed: (1) Positive — an authenticated user can access GET /create and receives 200, confirming the login_required decorator passes through for logged-in users; (2) Negative — an anonymous user gets exactly 302 to /auth/login, testing the core requirement; (3) Boundary/STC — a user who logs out (transitions from authenticated to anonymous) is then redirected on GET /create, confirming the state transition is respected. Each test asserts exact status codes and exact Location header values to kill operator-flip and constant-bump mutations.

tests.name: test_anonymous_get_create_redirects_to_login
preconditions: Application is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database
No user is logged in (no session cookie)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_anonymous_get_create_redirects_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/create')
    assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login', (
        f'Expected /auth/login, got {r.headers["Location"]}'
    )

test_anonymous_get_create_redirects_to_login()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_authenticated_get_create_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post(
        '/auth/login',
        data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'}
    )
    assert login_r.status_code == 302, f'Login failed: {login_r.status_code}'
    assert login_r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    r = client.get('/create')
    assert r.status_code == 200, (
        f'Expected 200 for authenticated user, got {r.status_code}'
    )

test_authenticated_get_create_returns_200()

tests.name: test_logged_out_user_get_create_redirects_to_login
preconditions: Application is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database
User Anjali (id=2, password=cloud) exists in the database
User logs in, then logs out — transitioning from authenticated to anonymous
expected: GET /create after logout returns HTTP 302 with Location=/auth/login
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_logged_out_user_get_create_redirects_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post(
        '/auth/login',
        data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'}
    )
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    create_while_logged_in = client.get('/create')
    assert create_while_logged_in.status_code == 200
    logout_r = client.get('/auth/logout')
    assert logout_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/create')
    assert r.status_code == 302, (
        f'Expected 302 after logout, got {r.status_code}'
    )
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login', (
        f'Expected /auth/login, got {r.headers["Location"]}'
    )

test_logged_out_user_get_create_redirects_to_login()
